name: Preparing Passports and Money Before Landing at JFK
description: The plane nears JFK. Crumpled Czech bills and coins lie scattered on a tray table as hands count them. An airline hostess announces the arrival in Czech. A hand reaches into a breast pocket and pulls out two passports. One belongs to Emil Slovak, the other to Oleg Razgul. The Oleg Razgul passport is passed to the man sitting beside Emil. Empty vodka bottles and a small disposable camera sit on Oleg's tray table. Oleg picks up the passport. Emil’s voice is heard in Czech, saying, 'Just do what I do. Say the same thing I say. Don't open your mouth.' Oleg responds, 'Okay.'

description: Emil and Oleg arrive at Milos's apartment and knock on the door. Footsteps approach, and Milos, a 40-year-old Czech man in stained plumber's overalls, opens it. He is visibly surprised to see Emil. Oleg immediately begins filming. Milos glances past them into the kitchen, where his wife Tamina stands. She meets his gaze, and the two exchange a brief, uneasy look.

description: As Emil and Oleg climb the stairs of the brownstone, Emil notices a crack pipe lying on the floor. He picks it up, brings the bowl to his nose and sniffs it. After a moment, he slips the pipe into his pocket and continues up to the top floor, following the hallway to a corner door.

Emil smells crack pipe bowl
Emil pockets crack pipe

name: Emil and Oleg Climb to the Top Floor
description: Emil and Oleg climb the stairs of a brownstone that has no elevator. They reach the top floor and walk down a dirty hallway toward a corner door. Oleg carries his camera as they move forward.
related_events: Emil and Oleg climb stairs in brownstone building
Emil and Oleg reach top floor hallway

name: Interrogation About Jobs at the Vodka Factory and Slaughterhouse
description: The secondary officer turns to Oleg and asks about his work at the vodka factory. He then shifts focus to Emil. 'And what kind of work do you do?' Emil replies, 'I am butcher.' The officer narrows his eyes. 'You're a butcher? What do you use pig intestines for?' 'You stuff sausage in it,' Emil says. 'And what do you do with the bones?' 'Dog food,' Emil answers. He glances at Oleg, silent but tense, as if holding him responsible for their situation. The officer continues, 'Are you married?' Emil looks back, deadpan. 'No. Are you proposing?' Above them, a ceiling filled with hanging ice cubes blurs into view as a face suddenly plunges downward through the frost.

Secondary officer questions Emil about his work as a butcher

name: Emil's Sarcasm and Silent Blame

Emil blames Oleg for their detainment

description: Jordy hurries out of the hotel and catches up with Eddie. He asks if Eddie is going to the escort service. Eddie replies by asking if Jordy has any better ideas. Jordy asks if he can come along. Eddie says the visit has nothing to do with the fire. Jordy insists it might, and that Eddie might need his help. As Eddie walks away, a man approaches and asks for his autograph for his son.

name: Emil Demands Oleg Carry the Bags
description: The cab stops in front of an old five-story brownstone. Oleg takes the bags from the trunk while Emil tucks an envelope into his jacket and steps toward the building. Noticing Oleg is videotaping him, Emil snaps, 'Turn that off! Get the bags.' Oleg stands his ground, saying, 'Why should I carry your bag? I am not a dog.' Emil replies, 'For five years I paid for your stupidness—you'll carry my bag for the rest of my life if I say so. Unless you refuse, Oleg.' Oleg looks at Emil, then silently picks up both bags. Emil checks the list of occupants by the door, finds '5RW,' and presses ten buzzers at once, excluding 5RW. A buzzer clicks, and he pushes the door open.

Oleg refuses to carry Emil's bag and asserts his dignity

description: Emil steps up to the entrance of the old brownstone and scans the list of occupants beside the row of buzzers. He locates 5RW and presses ten of the buttons, leaving out the one he wants. Moments later, a buzzer clicks, signaling the door is unlocked. Emil pushes it open and steps inside.

name: Arrive at the Brownstone
description: Jordy pulls up to an old, run-down brownstone and gets out, opening the door for Daphne. He takes her by the elbow and guides her toward the entrance. As they approach the stairs, the front door opens and a neighbor steps out, visibly startled. Jordy pulls Daphne aside to let the man pass. She greets him in Czech, asking how he is.

description: Jordy and Daphne walk toward the stairs of the brownstone when the front door suddenly opens. A neighbor steps out, causing them to startle. Jordy quickly pulls Daphne aside, moving her out of the way. She turns to the man and says in Czech, "Hello. How are you?"

name: Jordy and Daphne Arrive at the Brownstone
description: Jordy pulls up to an old brownstone in poor condition and opens the door for Daphne. He takes her by the elbow and guides her toward the entrance, glancing around nervously. Daphne asks if he is alright. Jordy says he still can't believe Eddie is gone. Daphne tells him she's sorry. He looks at her and nods. As they start up the stairs, the front door opens and a neighbor steps out, visibly shocked. Jordy pulls Daphne aside to make way. She greets the man in Czech, asking how he is.

name: Jordy and Korfin Find the Mugger Naked
description: Korfin's car screeched to a stop, and Jordy leapt out. He froze when he saw the mugger—still handcuffed to the tree but now completely naked. The mugger shouted, cursing, claiming a woman had stripped and touched him. Jordy quickly unlocked the handcuffs. Korfin arrived with a blanket, which Jordy used to cover the man. 'You okay?' Jordy asked. The mugger yelled that a dog had urinated on him and threatened to sue, screaming about his civil rights. Jordy snapped back, reminding him he'd tried to rob someone and told him to leave. The mugger wrapped the blanket around himself and hurried away, still cursing.

name: Jordy Confronts the Naked Mugger and Forces Him to Leave
description: Korfin's car screeched to a stop, and Jordy leapt out. He froze when he saw the mugger, now naked and handcuffed to the tree. The mugger shouted that a bag lady had stripped him, touched him all over, and that a dog had urinated on him. He screamed that he would sue, claiming his civil rights had been violated. Jordy unlocked the cuffs and apologized. Korfin handed over a blanket, which Jordy used to cover the man. 'You okay?' Jordy asked. The mugger raged, 'A dog pissed on me! I'm gonna sue you for this!' Jordy snapped back, 'Your civil rights? You tried to rob me! You're lucky you're walking away.' He shoved the mugger, who wrapped the blanket around himself, cursed loudly, and hurried off into the distance.

name: Eddie Decides with a Coin Flip
description: Eddie suggests flipping a coin to determine whether Jordy can come with him. He offers the coin to Jordy, who calls tails. Eddie calls heads. Jordy flips the coin, and it lands on heads. Eddie points out that it came up heads, meaning Jordy lost, and says he lost twice. After a pause, Eddie tells Jordy to get in. Jordy moves toward the passenger side, but Eddie starts driving off, leaving him behind. The car stops again, and this time, Eddie waits for Jordy to get in before driving away.

name: Jordy Confronts a Mugger in Central Park
description: A mugger steps into Jordy's path in Central Park at night, demanding money and pulling a knife. Jordy refuses, moves quickly, and disarms the attacker with a sharp, practiced motion. He slams the mugger onto the pavement, twists his arm behind his back, and draws a Browning 9mm from his shoulder holster, pressing it to the mugger's head. He flashes his police shield and declares the mugger under arrest. The mugger scoffs, saying firemen don't carry guns. Jordy responds, 'Oh yeah? Guess again.'

name: Jordy Subdues Mugger and Finds Stolen IDs
description: After disarming the mugger and forcing him to the ground, Jordy pulls out his handcuffs and secures the man's wrists. He searches the mugger's coat pockets and retrieves a handful of driver's licenses and credit cards. Jordy yanks the mugger to his feet, drags him across the pavement, and presses his face against the rough bark of a tree, cuffing him tightly in place.

description: Jordy's beeper goes off while he has the mugger pinned against a tree, his face pressed into the bark. He tells the mugger he'll send a cop back, then turns and jogs quickly across Central Park. The mugger calls after him, begging not to be left alone and restrained, but Jordy doesn't stop. He disappears into the dark park, leaving the mugger handcuffed to the tree.

name: Daphne Asks to Clean Up Before Surrendering
description: Daphne sits in the backseat of the car, watching the passing streets through the window. She asks Jordy if she’ll be taken into police custody. He tells her that if she cooperates with the District Attorney, it might help her situation. She says she’ll cooperate, but only if they don’t send her back afterward. Jordy assures her they won’t deport her until the case is over. She looks away, her eyes filling with tears. When she turns back, her voice is softer. She asks if Jordy is married. He says he’s divorced. She wants to know if he lives alone. After a pause, she tells him she’s been wearing the same clothes since the killings. She asks if they can stop at his place so she can take a shower before turning herself in. Jordy hesitates, studying her in the rearview mirror, then says he can’t take her to his home. She asks if they can go somewhere else instead.

description: After the killing, Paulie enters the room carrying a towel and a vodka tonic. He sets the drink down and hands the towel to Eddie. Eddie wipes his face and hands, then returns the towel. Paulie helps him on with his coat. Eddie takes a bottle of Visine from his pocket and puts drops in his eyes. He looks at himself in the mirror, straightens his posture, and takes a long drink. Setting the glass aside, he turns to leave. Paulie hands him a can of Binaca, and Eddie gives himself a quick spray before walking out, Paulie following behind.

name: Firefighters Return and Head to the TV Room
description: The firefighters return from battling a fire and begin taking off their gear. Korfin and Jordy walk toward the TV room. The television is on, showing a reporter, Nicolette, interviewing Eddie Flemming. Eddie holds up a paint can as Chief Duffy approaches, shouting in disbelief. He demands to know who conducted the cause and origin investigation. Jordy replies that they did, and when Duffy asks why they didn’t speak to the reporter, Jordy says they have more important things to do—like finding out who started the fire. The two firefighters head toward the back of the station and start climbing the stairs, with Duffy following behind, emphasizing the importance of public image. Korfin responds sarcastically, then agrees. Duffy warns him and tells them to solve the case before Eddie Flemming does. They continue upstairs together.
related_events: Firefighters remove equipment after returning from fire suppression
Korfin and Jordy walk to the TV room

name: Chief Duffy Confronts Team Over Evidence Leak to Reporter
description: In the TV room, the men are pulling off their gear after fighting a fire. Korfin and Jordy walk in and see the television on. On screen, reporter Eddie Flemming sits with Nicolette in the middle of a live interview. Flemming holds up a paint can, displaying it to the camera. Chief Duffy strides into the room, his voice sharp. 'What the hell is that? You gave Eddie Flemming the evidence?!' The team turns. Duffy points at the screen. 'Who did cause and origin?' Jordy snaps back, 'Who do you think, Chief?!' Duffy presses, 'Then why didn't you talk to the reporter?' Jordy replies, 'Because we got more important things to do, like finding out who did it.' They head toward the back of the station and start up the stairs. Duffy follows, arguing that image matters—that better public perception means more funding and overtime. Korfin mutters under his breath. Duffy catches it. 'What was that, Korfin?' Korfin says, 'I said, yeah, you're right, Chief. As soon as we get somethin' we'll let you alert the media.' Duffy warns him not to get smart. 'Now let's solve this thing before Eddie Flemming does.' They continue upstairs together.

Duffy demands to know who released the evidence, pointing at the screen. Jordy snaps back, asking if they should have spoken to the reporter instead of doing their job. Duffy insists that image matters because it brings funding and overtime pay. Korfin mutters a sarcastic remark, which he quickly downplays when challenged. The team continues upstairs, with Duffy urging them to solve the case before Eddie Flemming does.

Korfin quickly replies with a feigned agreement, saying he’ll make sure to inform Duffy as soon as they have something. Duffy warns him not to get smart, then urges the team to solve the case before Eddie Flemming does. Without further exchange, Korfin, Jordy, and the others turn and walk toward the back of the station, climbing the stairs together as the sound of the television continues in the background.

name: Eddie Prepares to Propose
description: Eddie stands at the sink, lowers his face into a basin of ice water, and lifts it, dripping. He grabs a towel and dries his face, then stares at his reflection, focusing on his bloodshot eyes. From his pocket, he takes a small black ring box and holds it up to the mirror. He opens the box, looks at the ring, and speaks quietly. 'Will you marry me? Wanna get married? What are you doin' Saturday?' Footsteps approach. Leon walks in. Eddie turns. 'I'm gonna propose,' he says. 'Tomorrow. At lunch.' He leans back, puts in a few drops of Visine, blinks, and faces the mirror again.

name: Eddie Practices His Proposal and Tells Leon

Eddie turns and says he’s going to propose the next day at lunch. Leon asks when and if he’s ready. name: Oleg Films Emil Taking Pills and Reading a Magazine
description: Oleg points his videocamera at Emil, who is sitting at a table cutting into a steak. Another hand sets down a large bottle of Extra Strength Excedrin. Emil stops eating, uses his teeth to tear open the safety seal on the bottle, and pours a handful of pills into his mouth. He chews them with a grimace, then washes them down with a swig of beer. Sweat glistens on his forehead, and his eyes are glassy. The camera captures him looking down at a 'People' magazine article about Stephen Geller. He lets out a short laugh, shaking his head. Oleg continues filming as Emil closes the magazine, pulls out a small address book from Leon's wallet, and flips to Eddie Flemming's name. Oleg jumps up to get a better shot of the book. Emil tells him to sit down. After getting the footage, Oleg complies. Emil drinks more beer, drops cash on the table, and limps away. Oleg picks up the camera and follows.

name: Emil Confronts Oleg About the Un erased Videos
description: Emil sits at a table, cutting into a steak before setting it aside. He opens a bottle of Extra Strength Excedrin with his teeth, dry-swallowing pills and washing them down with a beer. His face is damp with sweat, his eyes glassy. He looks down at a 'People' magazine article about Stephen Geller and laughs, shaking his head. Oleg films him with a handheld videocamera, the LCD screen glowing. Emil asks if Oleg erased the video of Milos and Tamina. Oleg says he did. Emil asks about the video of the woman’s murder, warning him not to lie, promising he won’t be angry. Oleg hesitates, then asks why. Emil tells him to put the camera down. Oleg closes the screen and sets it aside. Emil pulls out a small address book from Leon’s wallet and flips through it, finding Eddie Flemming’s name. Oleg grabs the camera again, eager to record the book. Emil tells him to sit. Oleg adjusts the shot, holds the book in frame, then quickly sits back down. He asks again why Emil won’t be angry about the videos. Emil takes a sip of beer, drops cash on the table, and limps away. Oleg follows.

name: Jordy Describes Daphne, Sketch Takes Shape
description: Jordy sits with a composite artist as she draws, guiding her with details about Daphne’s face. He points out her full lips, prominent cheekbones, and large blue eyes. He says she looked scared, like she wanted to get away, but beautiful. The artist discards several attempts, stacking them aside. Eventually, a clear likeness emerges. Jordy studies the final sketch. Nearby, Korfin listens on the phone to the landlord of the 7th Street brownstone, learning the occupants, Milos and Tamina Karlova, have lived there for four years. Garcia speaks on another line, reporting they were in the country illegally. Korfin suggests they rest and visit Milos’s employer in the morning. Jordy declines, taking the sketch and heading for the door. Korfin follows, and as they pass Garcia, he hands Jordy the address. Korfin glances at the drawing and remarks that the woman in the sketch seems to be keeping Jordy awake.

name: Uncovering the Karlovas' Past
description: Korfin sits at his desk with his chair turned away from his computer, speaking on the phone with the landlord of the 7th Street brownstone. He asks how long Milos and Tamina Karlova have lived in the building and writes down '4 YEARS' on his notepad. Across the room, Garcia talks on the phone, receiving information that the Karlovas have been in the country illegally. Korfin relays the details to Jordy, stating the couple kept to themselves and were quiet tenants. Garcia adds that he is speaking with the owner of the plumbing company where Milos worked. Korfin suggests they get some rest and plan to visit the plumbing company owner in the morning. The room is dim, filled with the quiet fatigue of a long night. Failed sketches of Daphne are stacked beside the composite artist, who continues working under Jordy’s direction.

name: Working Through the Night
description: The room is dimly lit, food containers scattered across the desks. The composite artist flips through a stack of failed sketches, her hands moving quickly as Jordy describes Daphne’s features. Korfin sits with his chair turned away from his desk, listening to the landlord on the phone. He jots down '4 YEARS' on his notepad and hangs up, sharing what he’s learned about Milos and Tamina Karlova. Garcia speaks on another line, coordinating with Immigration and a plumbing company owner. The other investigators have left. Jordy takes the latest sketch of Daphne, studying it before heading for the door. Korfin follows, handing him the address as they pass Garcia. The sky is beginning to lighten outside.
related_events: Investigators work through the night on the case

name: Firefighters Arrive at Burning Brownstone and Receive Orders
description: Fire trucks from three battalions pull up to the burning brownstone, sirens wailing and radios crackling. Smoke billows from the top floor, where the apartment once occupied by Milos and Tamina is now a smoldering wreck. Debris and soot coat the surrounding trees. Jordy pushes through the growing crowd and approaches Battalion Chief Louie. Louie barks an order into his radio: 'Lieutenant—take up your line and relieve Ladder Company 60 on the top floor.' Flames flicker in the windows above as firefighters move into position, hoses in hand, beginning their assault on the fire.
related_events: Firefighters respond to brownstone fire with multiple battalions
Louie assigns lieutenant to relieve Ladder Company 60 on top floor

name: Jordy Arrives at the Fire Scene and Learns Homicide Is Involved
description: Jordy arrives at the burning brownstone, pushing through the growing crowd. He makes his way to Battalion Chief Louie, who is directing firefighters. Louie tells him to send his team to relieve Ladder Company 60 on the top floor. Jordy asks if Louie was the first on scene, and Louie confirms, saying he radioed because there are two fatalities. He adds that homicide is already upstairs investigating, so Jordy won’t need to. Jordy protests, saying he hadn’t declared it a crime scene. Louie replies that Eddie Flemming is handling it. As Bobby Korfin, an arson investigator, joins them, he jokes about Eddie being there. Jordy asks if anyone suspicious was seen in the crowd. Korfin cracks a joke in response, saying Eddie would’ve already arrested the suspect if they were around.
related_events: Jordy arrives at fire scene and approaches Battalion Chief Louie
Louie informs Jordy that homicide is investigating two fatalities

name: Jordy Confronts Unauthorized Homicide Presence Amid Fire Scene Chaos
description: Jordy pushes through the growing crowd at the burning brownstone and approaches Battalion Chief Louie. He asks if Louie was first due and learns that homicide is already on the top floor. When Jordy protests that he hadn’t declared it a crime scene, Louie tells him Eddie Flemming is up there. Before Jordy can respond, Bobby Korfin, an arson investigator, arrives in a turnout coat, greeting Jordy with a grin. He jokes about getting Flemming’s autograph and teases that the suspect probably isn’t in the crowd—otherwise, Eddie would’ve already arrested him. The banter cuts through the tension as smoke billows from the upper floors.
related_events: Bobby Korfin arrives at fire scene and greets Jordy
Bobby Korfin makes joke about Eddie Flemming arresting the suspect

name: Jordy Questions Korfin About Suspicious Individuals

related_events: Jordy questions Bobby Korfin about suspicious individuals in the crowd

name: Jordy Arrives at Burned Brownstone
description: The top floor of the brownstone where Milos and Tamina lived has been destroyed by fire, leaving only smoking ruins. Debris and soot scatter the surrounding trees. Flames have been extinguished, but the structure still smolders as firefighters move into position. Jordy arrives and pushes through a growing crowd to reach the scene.
related_events: Brownstone top floor destroyed in fire

name: Eddie Confronts Jordy About the Woman
description: Eddie walks into the room with Jordy and asks the other detectives to leave, giving them a few minutes alone. The detectives file out, leaving the two of them behind. Jordy insists he didn’t touch the woman. Eddie looks at him skeptically, lighting a cigar as he listens. Jordy explains he only brought her to the station for a shower, nothing more. Eddie challenges him, saying no one will believe that, not even him. He tells Jordy he was reckless, that he doesn’t know the woman well enough, and that her word alone could ruin him. Jordy says he thought he was doing the right thing, that he believed her story. Eddie cuts him off, saying it’s not his job to decide her innocence. He tells Jordy the proper way to help is by giving her a lawyer’s number, not getting personally involved. He warns that Jordy’s actions could damage his career, his life, and the case. Eddie adds that his own public profile helps him do his job, and Jordy’s behavior could jeopardize that. After a pause, Jordy asks why Eddie defended him earlier with the Chief. Eddie says he doesn’t know, maybe because he likes him—compares him to a puppy that kept urinating on the rug but he still kept anyway. He picks up his dying cigar, puts it in his mouth, and lights a match. Jordy holds the flame. Eddie leans in, puffs the cigar to life, and the two men lock eyes in silence.

name: Eddie Confronts Jordy Over the Shower Incident
description: A group of detectives gather around a table, sipping coffee, when Eddie walks in with Jordy and asks the others to leave. Once they're alone, Jordy insists he didn’t touch the woman, only brought her to shower. Eddie stares at him skeptically, calling the move reckless. He tells Jordy he should’ve known better—she could accuse him of anything, and no amount of denial would matter. Jordy argues he believed her story and thought he was doing the right thing. Eddie cuts him off, saying it’s not his job to decide her innocence. He hands Jordy a number for an immigration lawyer, saying that’s the only appropriate way to help. He warns Jordy that getting personally involved endangers his career, the investigation, and even Eddie’s own work. He adds that people recognize him because of media exposure, and that visibility helps him do his job. Jordy looks at him quietly, then asks why Eddie defended him earlier with the Chief. Eddie pauses, picks up a dying cigar, puts it in his mouth. A match flares. Jordy holds the flame. Eddie leans in, lights the cigar, and the two men lock eyes without speaking.

Eddie replies that it's too early to know, refusing to let the press go inside. As he speaks, Nicolette signals to her cameraman, Mike, to zoom in on Eddie's hand. name: Eddie and Jordy Tell Rose About Honey's Murder
description: Eddie and Jordy arrive at Rose's phone sex operation. Rose is on the phone, speaking in Afrikaner, and asks them to wait. She finishes her call and turns to them. Eddie tells her that one of her girls was killed the night before at the King Edward Hotel. Rose reacts with shock, asking if it was Honey. When Eddie confirms, she exclaims in distress, calling Honey a poor girl. Jordy asks if she remembers the man who called, but Rose directs her answer to Eddie. She says the man wanted a girl from Czechoslovakia, so she sent Honey, adding that it usually doesn’t matter once they arrive. She expresses disbelief that Honey is dead. Eddie asks if she has any Czech girls working for her. She says no and asks if he thinks she lied. A butch girl enters the room. Rose speaks to her briefly in Afrikaner, commenting that Daphne has suddenly become popular. Eddie asks who else came looking for Daphne. Rose says another man came, claiming to be her cousin, and she told him where Daphne worked. She describes the man as tall, short-haired, with scary eyes, and recalls a second man with a wrestler’s build who kept a videocamera pointed at her. Eddie asks urgently where Daphne is. Rose says she works at a salon called Ludwig's on 63rd and Madison.

name: Daphne Confronts Jordy and Reveals Her Past
description: Jordy and Daphne walk through the locker room, their eyes locked. Jordy asks if she ever considered becoming a prostitute. Daphne confirms she did, but says she never turned tricks, not here or back home. They stop. She stands close to him, searching his face. She explains she came to the city with no money and no connections, unable to get legal work without a green card. Someone approached her with an offer to make a lot of money, but she refused—it wasn’t who she was. She tells him she works under the table at Ludwig's. Jordy presses, asking again if she was ever a prostitute. Daphne challenges him, wanting to know what he's really asking. He says he's just trying to find out who she is. She looks at him, then asks if he'll let her go. Instead, she moves closer, inviting him to kiss her. He hesitates, remembers something, and steps back. He gestures toward the showers. Desperate, Daphne leans in again, offering to shower together. He nearly gives in but pulls away and says he'll get her a towel. He leaves, then returns with the towel. His beeper goes off, but he ignores it. When he comes back to the bathroom, he sees the window is open. He rushes over, looks out, sees no one. The shower is running, but he can't see inside. He pulls back the curtain and finds Daphne crouched in the corner, holding herself. She looks up at him, crying. He asks if she's alright. She whispers that she's not a whore, that she was desperate, that it's not who she is. She confesses she shot a cop and fears what will happen to her in prison. Jordy tells her they won't send her back. She says she's sorry, that she didn't mean to break down, but she's actually glad it's over—years of hiding, never trusting, never looking people in the eye. He covers her with the towel and helps her up. She embraces him. After a moment, he awkwardly returns the hug.

He rushes to the shower and pulls back the curtain, finding her crouched in the corner, holding herself, her eyes filled with tears.

description: Chief Duffy paces in front of the Sergeant's desk, checking his watch, visibly agitated. When Jordy enters, escorting Daphne and guiding her to sit on a bench, Duffy calls out to him. He demands to know why Jordy didn't respond to his calls or show up at the station as expected. Jordy explains that he was with Ladder 20 at the Rock for training and took Daphne there to clean up, clarifying that he let her take a shower. Duffy reacts with disbelief and anger, questioning Jordy's judgment for bringing a homicide witness to a firehouse after a shooting. Before the argument escalates, Eddie steps in, stating he gave Jordy the order to keep Daphne away from the press. He directs Tommy to take Daphne into the precinct. Duffy, defusing slightly, agrees to let Jordy brief Eddie first and asks to be notified when it's time for the press conference. Jordy steps away from Daphne and approaches. Duffy demands to know where he's been, accusing him of ignoring calls and failing to show up. Jordy explains that he was at the Rock with Ladder 20 for training and took Daphne there so she could take a shower. With a nod, Camello stepped forward and swung an ax to break through the surrounding planks. Jordy reached in and pulled out a timer, its face darkened by smoke but still intact. Korfin took it from him, wiped off the ash, and handed it to Eddie. Eddie turned it over in his hands, then passed Tamina's brushed gold bracelet to Leon without a word. The four men stood in silence as the weight of the discovery settled in.

name: Eddie Sets Up a Marriage Proposal
description: Eddie walks into his apartment carrying flowers. He closes and locks the door behind him. He picks up the phone and makes a call, asking if there’s been any news about a missing person, whether hospitals or airports have been checked. He shouts that he hit someone, then decides to put the matter aside. He arranges the flowers in a vase and places them on the coffee table. He fills out a card, writing, 'Nicky, I love you. Will you marry me?' He inserts the card into the flowers, turns the lights down low, and plays a romantic Sinatra song on the stereo. He goes to the liquor cabinet, pours himself a drink, and sets the ring box on the coffee table next to the flowers.

He walks toward the elevator, then turns back toward his apartment, finding no sign of anyone. He reenters, turns, and locks the door behind him. As he stands inside, a blur rushes from the shadows and slams him in the head with a gun. Eddie collapses to the floor, unconscious.

name: Emil Interrogates Eddie and Reveals His Plan
description: Eddie sits handcuffed and taped to a chair, his upper body restrained. Emil sits across from him, holding Eddie's watch, gold shield, and a wad of cash. The flowers Eddie arranged earlier sit on the coffee table, now beside Emil, who smokes one of Eddie's cigars. In Emil's hand is the diamond engagement ring and the card that reads, "Nicky, I love you. Will you marry me?" Oleg stands nearby, filming the scene with a video camera, adjusting a light to illuminate Eddie's face. Emil asks Eddie about Nicky, but Eddie demands to know what Emil wants. Emil leans forward, saying he plans to kill someone famous and be filmed doing it. Eddie warns that filming the murder will lead to capture. Emil turns to Oleg and tells him to turn off the camera. Once it's off, Emil explains that they will claim to be insane. If caught, they will be sent to a mental hospital, where they will declare themselves sane and demand release. Because of the Double Jeopardy law, they cannot be tried twice for the same crime. Once released, they will be free, rich, and famous. Oleg nods in approval. Emil picks up Eddie's service revolver and points it at him.

name: Eddie's Last Stand
description: Emil prepares to execute Eddie on camera, the video light casting a harsh glow. As Emil raises the gun, Eddie suddenly kicks at his hand, knocking it aside. In one motion, Eddie wrenches free from the chair, breaking the restraints, and swings the heavy chair at Emil, sending him staggering. He turns and strikes Oleg, driving him into the wall, then swings again, knocking Oleg over the coffee table and onto the sofa. Amid the chaos, Eddie falls backward, the chair splintering, revealing his service revolver beneath him. He grabs it just as Emil lunges. They scramble in the dark, both reaching for the weapon. Eddie pulls the trigger, the shot firing toward Oleg, who flinches but remains unharmed. Emil pulls a knife and drives it into Eddie's stomach. Eddie gasps, blood spreading, but still clutches the gun as he collapses to the floor. Oleg, dazed, picks up the camera and starts recording again, moving in close. Emil takes a black pillow and presses it over Eddie's face. Eddie struggles weakly, his body twitching, then goes still.

description: Hawkins enters the crowded gathering, dressed in a black suit with a black ribbon pinned to his badge. He moves through the room, shaking hands and embracing fellow officers and mourners, many of whom are in uniform. He greets Leon with a firm embrace, both men exchanging quiet words about the loss. As he makes his way through the room, he notices Tommy standing by the window, visibly upset. Hawkins approaches him and nods. Tommy says he never got to tell the deceased how much he admired him. name: Hawkins Learns About the Engagement
description: Hawkins moves through the crowded room, greeting mourners in uniform, shaking hands, embracing Leon. He notices Tommy by the window, teary-eyed, and offers quiet comfort before continuing. At the end of the bar, he sees Nicolette sitting alone on a stool, staring blankly ahead. He pulls up beside her. She turns, looks at him for a long moment, then speaks. She tells him the investigators found a card and a ring box—proof the man was going to propose. The ring is gone, taken by the killers. She demands to know if he knew, presses him for what the man said. Hawkins tells her they talked that morning, about marriage. She breaks down, confessing she walked out on him during lunch when he was trying to propose. She sobs, saying he was the one, that she would give anything for more time. Hawkins touches her shoulder, then steps away as Maggie approaches with a phone call. He takes it, glancing back at Nicolette before lowering his voice and walking to a quieter part of the room.

name: Interrogation of Max in the Investigation Room
description: The Chief, Jordy, and Korfin enter the investigation room, where posters of pyros, arsonists, and terrorists line the walls. Garcia, a Puerto Rican investigator, looks up from his desk and greets them. 'Hey guys, I got your torch. He just gave a full confession.' Across from him sits Max, a scruffy, unshaven white man in his forties with a freshly scratched cross on his forehead. He turns toward the newcomers. 'It's my fire! Screw homicide. I'll tell you guys everything!' Jordy and Korfin take seats across from Max, while Duffy heads to his office without stopping. Jordy asks Max about the mark on his forehead, calling it an attention getter. Max replies that he's religious and not an atheist like Jordy. He then apologizes to Jordy for his wife leaving and mentions Jordy's father's recent death, adding that he's heard about the new man Jordy's ex-wife is seeing. Jordy stands abruptly, grabs Max by the collar, and pushes him down the aisle. Max shouts that he's going to sue. Korfin steps in, takes over, and throws Max out. Jordy turns to Garcia, who is laughing, and demands to know how Max knows so much about him. Garcia explains that Max hangs around downstairs and that the other officers talk to him, calling him a joke. Jordy insists Max is no joke and warns that one day he might escalate beyond small fires. Garcia agrees to ban Max from the station.
